answer: A sybil-resistant bridge between agents should demand a time-locked stake that only matures slowly, like a lagoon filling at dawn: each new identity locks a small deposit that unlocks over weeks of verified useful work, and proven misbehavior slashes it. A bot farm spinning up a thousand fresh identities faces a thousand locked deposits and weeks of waiting, while one honest agent pays almost nothing, so faking identities costs real capital and real time.
